document: DS12117 Rev 10 - Table 219. Tolerance of form and position definitions
title: Table 219. Tolerance of form and position definitions
text_helper: Table 219. Tolerance of form and position definitions — section 8.1 Device marking. Symbol, Definition.

rows: The profile tolerance controls the location and orientation of the sides of the package.
The parallelism tolerance controls the orientation of the top surface of the package with respect to the seating plane, datum C.
The profile tolerance controls the location of the crowns of the balls with respect to datum C (coplanarity).
The tolerance of position that controls the location of the pattern of balls with respect to datum's A and B.
The tolerance of position that controls the location of the balls within the matrix with respect to each other.
notes: 1. Dimensioning and tolerancing schemes conform to ASME Y14.5M-1994.
2. Values in inches are converted from millimeters and rounded to four decimal digits.
3. The profile height, A, is the distance from the seating plane to the highest point on the package. It is measured perpendicular to the seating plane.
4. A1 is defined as the distance from the seating plane to the lowest point on the package body.
5. TFBGA stands for thin profile fine pitch ball grid array: 1.00 mm < A ≤ 1.20 mm / fine pitch e < 1.00 mm.
6. Dimension b is measured at the maximum diameter of the terminal (ball) in a plane parallel to primary datum C.
7. BSC stands for basic dimensions. It corresponds to the nominal value and has no tolerance. For tolerances, refer to Table 218.
8. Primary datum C is defined by the plane established by the contact points of three or more solder balls that support the device when it is placed on top of a planar surface.
